policy_events.scope: aggregate rare-earth export quota, not per-element allotment
policy_events.driver: USGS historical reported restriction associated with price shock; do not assign entire price change to quota causally.

policy_events.event: Major rare-earth price spike followed by subsequent declines; 2010/11 controls and tight supply are historical price-story anchors.
policy_events.driver: IEA reported market episode; ingredient price agent supplies annual or market-specific series.

policy_events.event: WTO adopted appellate/panel reports in DS431 concerning China's REE export restrictions.
China notified WTO DSB of removal of export quotas, export duties and trading-right restrictions; U.S. questioned complete compliance.
Another price spike under tight supply conditions.
policy_events.driver: IEA assessment; no single-event causal claim supplied.

policy_events.event: Technology catalogue made specified REE extraction/separation, metal/alloy and magnet preparation technologies prohibited exports, with other REE mining/beneficiation/smelting/extractant technologies restricted.
policy_events.status: effective baseline technology regime; July 2025 partial amendment is separate

policy_events.event: Kachin border closures disrupted Myanmar raw-material routes into China; gradual reopening in 2025.
policy_events.driver: IEA reported governance/supply disruption; combined heavy magnet-REE basis, not separate Dy/Tb volumes.

policy_events.event: Announcement 18 immediately instituted licenses for listed medium/heavy REE metals, alloys, oxides, compounds and related products, including Dy/Tb-containing NdFeB materials.
policy_events.status: effective licensing; still separate from later suspension

policy_events.event: Announcements 57/61/62 expanded element products, some foreign-made/re-export product reach, and technology/personnel-related licensing; No61's foreign-made value/technology provisions were dated to start Dec1, other parts immediate.
Announcement70 immediately suspended Nos55,56,57,58,61,62 through Nov10 2026; No18 absent from suspension list.
policy_events.status: effective suspension, numbered text still displays this date

policy_events.event: All dual-use exports prohibited to Japanese military users, military uses and other end uses enhancing Japan's military capability; Chinese-origin third-country transfers also covered.
policy_events.status: effective end-user/end-use restriction; not a blanket civilian Japan ban

policy_events.event: MOFCOM Announcement 23 adds ten U.S. entities including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to export-control list.
policy_events.status: effective immediately; no later removal/suspension located in searched primary sources as of 2026-10-07
policy_events.scope: Ban on dual-use exports to named entities; third-country organizations/persons may not transfer/provide Chinese-origin dual-use items to them. Special-case application provision. Not a blanket embargo on every rare-earth product.
policy_events.driver: Separate named-end-user restriction, not covered simply by October 2025 expansion's suspension.

policy_events.event: White House says rare-earth/critical-mineral supply shortages remain under discussion with objective of restoring appropriate shipment levels.
policy_events.status: summit statement, not repeal or shipment guarantee

policy_events.event: MOFCOM announced extension of Kuala Lumpur joint arrangement to Jan10 2027; rare-earth notices not individually named.
policy_events.status: political extension; numbered-notice implementation evidence gap

policy_events.event: DFARS magnet restriction extends to mined/refined/separated stages; NdFeB chain described from Nd/Fe/B mining through finished magnets. Specified exceptions/waivers remain.
policy_events.status: enacted future effective date as of Oct7; defence procurement scope

security_decision_frame.objective: Maintain specified U.S. qualified service deliveries during a specified disruption under fixed budget B.
required_inputs: Required magnet grade/shape/qualification and allowable substitutions
Accessible oxide/metal/alloy/magnet inventories and conversion rates/yields
Stage-specific incremental capex/opex, qualification cost and lead time

options.benefit: Adds primary feed after permitting/ramp-up and can improve geographic diversity.
options.tradeoff: Feed element distribution and separation compatibility matter; mine investment can help where feed constrains future qualified delivery.
options.status: Mechanism/hypothesis to model, not blanket ranking

options.benefit: Converts accessible feed into usable end products.
options.tradeoff: Must cost the complete required path and trace readiness/customer acceptance. Downstream bottleneck alone does not prove mine spending never helps.
options.status: Mechanism supported by observed multi-stage projects

options.benefit: Potential near-term bridge for short disruptions.
options.tradeoff: An oxide stock cannot immediately satisfy a finished-part shortage without conversion and qualification. Compare oxide, metal, alloy, unfinished-magnet and qualified-part inventories, their carrying costs, and their interchangeability.

options.benefit: Swarf routes demonstrate early feed recovery; end-of-life access may grow later.
options.tradeoff: Collection, composition, recovery yield, conversion and qualification constrain available service; distinguish oxide recovery from direct magnet recycling.
options.status: Demonstrated technical routes; national impact unquantified

options.benefit: Can reduce HREE intensity or magnet dependence.
options.tradeoff: Application performance, thermal envelope, size/weight and customer requalification determine feasibility/time.
options.status: Candidate options, no assumed universal drop-in replacement

security_decision_frame.ranking: No national intervention ranking or shortage forecast: B, horizon and service requirements are not supplied.
